title: ROTAN: A Rotation-based Temporal Attention Network for Time-Specific Next POI Recommendation

problem.claim: Next POI recommendation must capture users' personalized sequential transitions in check-in trajectories to predict subsequent movements.

gap.claim: Most existing next POI recommendation studies ignore temporal information.

contributions.claim: The paper investigates time-specific next POI recommendation by incorporating target time information.
Time2Rotation represents timeslots as rotation vectors and applies rotation operations to capture temporal information.
ROTAN is a rotation-based temporal attention network for time-specific next POI recommendation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Time2Rotation as brand new and ROTAN as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets.
The authors report that the experiments demonstrate advantages of Time2Rotation and ROTAN.

narrative_sequence.summary: Next POI recommendation predicts users' subsequent movements and requires modeling personalized sequential transitions.
Existing studies generally omit temporal information.
The paper introduces time-specific next POI recommendation with target time information.
Time2Rotation encodes timeslots as rotation vectors, and ROTAN uses them in a temporal attention network with graph-based and trajectory-level modeling.
Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate advantages of the proposed technique and model.

source_observation.claim: The proposed approach represents timeslots as rotation vectors and applies rotation operations.

interpretation.claim: A geometric representation may provide a mechanism for incorporating temporal structure into sequential recommendation.

application.claim: When sequential behavior depends on time, evaluate representations that encode temporal relations directly rather than treating time as unrelated metadata.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether rotation-based time encoding is beneficial across settings beyond the reported experiments.

source_observation.claim: ROTAN separately represents user preference and POI influence while modeling individual check-in trajectories.

interpretation.claim: Separating distinct sources of sequential influence may help represent different temporal patterns.

application.claim: For personalized sequential prediction, consider modeling user-related and item-related influences as distinct components when their temporal behavior differs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how the separate representations are trained or whether the separation improves performance independently.

unknowns: The names and characteristics of the three datasets are not provided.
Evaluation metrics, baselines, numerical results, and statistical comparisons are not provided.
Implementation details and reproducibility information are not provided.
